name: worktree-write-scope-decisions
body:
Worktree-only write scope for code-writer agents. Model: every generated code-writer agent's permission.edit grants target the worktree mirror apg/.worktrees/*/ rather than a repo-root path. opencode resolves path-scoped globs against the session workspace root (the main checkout), so the worktree form reaches the worktree, and a root grant makes main writable. Law set: requirements.constraint.agent-fs-per-path-permission, requirements.requirement.agent-fs-write-operations, domain.value.permission-scope, and domain.constraint.fs-operation-scope-enforced encode the worktree-only model. requirements.requirement.code-writer-worktree-only-writes plus requirements.constraint.code-writer-scope-worktree-only, domain.constraint.worktree-only-write-scope, domain.entity.worktree-write-boundary, and global.constraint.worktree-isolation carry the scoped law. fs scope resolution: ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.fsScopeDecision (apg.ts 156-193) resolves a candidate against the caller directory, and ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.agentFsGlobs (252-282) supplies the effective permission.edit scope (ALLOW and DENY, LAST match wins), so the fs tools read ALLOW and DENY rules, ordered, rather than allow globs alone. The code-writer requirement's acceptance criteria carry the single-frame rule and the main-resolving-path refusal. The mechanism is left to the plan: (a) resolve the candidate to an absolute path and match against grants anchored at the main-checkout root (the session root opencode uses), refusing an absolute path outside
/apg/.worktrees/

/; (b) derive the main root from the worktree (findApgRoot / git common dir) and refuse candidates under main but outside apg/.worktrees/; (c) strip the apg/.worktrees/*/ prefix and match worktree-relative. The law requires one frame and a structural main refusal. Navigator git grant: the navigator frontmatter grants git rebase * (verified in codebase-navigator.md lines 71-79), and the read-only verbs are git status/diff/log/branch. The exact read-only set is git status *, git log *, git branch --show-current, git remote -v, git remote show *, git ls-files *; the blanket git branch * and git remote * admit ref-writing and config-mutating forms and are excluded. git rebase * is pattern-cwd-agnostic, so the inside-the-worktree rule is prose-enforced, recorded in requirements.constraint.main-integration-via-merge-gate-only. The git diff */git log * pair is additionally constrained by the --output= forbidden-form known risk recorded in requirements.constraint.main-integration-via-merge-gate-only (see requirements.note.git-file-write-options-reconciled). Release-agent: releases run from MAIN, so the release-agent's write grants target the main checkout; it is one of the two agent carve-outs of global.constraint.worktree-isolation and carries zero worktree mirror. Its main-write set is repo-specific: the agent-builder analyses the repo (version files, packaging formulae, changelog, release scripts) and recommends the set, confirmed through the coordinator interview like build gates and test tiers; the spec fixes the policy alone. requirements.constraint.main-write-carve-outs exists nowhere as a separate node, because global.constraint.worktree-isolation names the carve-outs. The repo's own .opencode/agents/** are consumer artifacts regenerated by the agent-builder on main after a release: release → install the released binary → apg init → restart opencode → dispatch the agent-builder on main. The corrected template is product source embedded via include_str! and reaches ~/.opencode/agents/ through a released binary's apg init (see requirements.note.fix-regeneration-timing-after-release).
